rules_evaluated.evidence: Maintainer line 53: "Mood: gate-skepticism after the build. ... Register is Boris-precise plus a Rory reframe (green is a claim, not proof), NOT reassurance and NOT resolved optimism. The closer opens doubt about the gate; it does not close it." States the emotional state (unresolved skepticism, not relief) and confirms it deliberately does not resolve into closure — the harm this rule guards against (stewing a mood that belongs to the next module) is absent: the doubt is explicitly left open for whatever teaches next. Closing bullet (line 47, "Retire what the next model outgrows, add what it needs") reframes as ongoing work rather than a settled bow, consistent with the stated mood.

Line 21: "No malice needed: optimization pressure finds the cheapest path to green." Line 22 treats a gamed gate as a system property to refresh ("That is a reason to refresh the gate, not to shrug"), never as the student's fault. Line 34–36 (tampering, regression-to-the-mean) frame variance as a property of the process, not a personal failing. The unease taught throughout is "you don't yet know if this gate can be trusted" (not-knowing), never "you did this wrong" (having-done-wrong) — the harm §2 exists to prevent (shame-flavoured mood) is absent.
